name: Northwest Couloir (Cedar Creek approach)
approach: From Highway 20 near Winthrop, reach the Cedar Creek Trailhead (reported at 2,961 ft elevation) and follow the Cedar Creek Trail before leaving it to bushwhack cross-country toward Cedar Creek; a known ford crossing (via a log in some years, a wade in others) gives access to the Shelokum Creek drainage, which is followed trail-less uphill to open meadows/snowfields below the northwest couloir.

waypoints.name: Cedar Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: USFS Trail #476 trailhead off SR-20 near milepost 175-176, west of Winthrop.
waypoints.directions: From Winthrop, drive about 17 miles west on SR 20 (or about 115 miles east from Burlington) and turn south on FR 200, signed for Cedar Creek. Drive 0.8 mile to the trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issued wilderness permit is available at the trailhead.

permit: Free self-issue Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness permit at the trailhead; no quota or fee. Northwest Forest Pass at developed trailheads.
pro_tips: This couloir has been skied in good snow years.
Following an existing GPX track (several are shared by past climbers) significantly eases the trail-less sections west of Cedar Creek.
Staying just west of the creek on the approach minimizes bushwhacking, per a 2024 trip report.
watch_out: Cedar Creek can become un-fordable after hot weather increases snowmelt — one party was forced to split up and camp separately when the creek proved too dangerous to cross as a group.
Snow conditions on the couloir vary from soft and easy to hard ice depending on recent freeze-thaw — carry crampons and an axe (a second axe was wished for in one trip report).
